Brick Occupancy Recomputation is a GPU compute shader routine that regenerates the occupancy status of volumetric bricks after dynamic voxel changes, ensuring the hierarchical traversal structure remains consistent with the underlying voxel data [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that a compute shader is used to recompute brick occupancy after voxel changes (caused by the player or cellular automata). It details the mechanism: thread blocks with 32 threads, each reading 16 voxels, counting non-air voxels, storing counts in shared memory, synchronizing, and having the first thread sum these counts to update the brickmap. This confirms the claim that the routine regenerates occupancy status to maintain consistency with voxel data.
